open_points.subject: start-up cleanup of unpublished trial fixtures
open_points.text: The data directory has “a content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest”, but start-up removes only “value bytes no record names”; a failed call may leave “a published file no record names”.
open_points.question: When adding or capturing a trial case publishes a file fixture but the store call fails before recording it, must the unreferenced fixture be removed at the next start, retained indefinitely, or treated as a start failure?
options: Remove every unreferenced content-addressed file, including file fixtures
Remove only unreferenced value bytes and retain unreferenced fixtures
Refuse to start when an unreferenced fixture is found
open_points.default_guess: Remove every unreferenced content-addressed file, including file fixtures.

open_points.subject: failure to remove unreferenced value bytes
open_points.text: “On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names … are removed”; only a spool-directory failure is then defined: “A spool directory that cannot be removed does not stop the start”.
open_points.question: What happens when an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be removed: does start fail, does the kernel start while never serving it, or is another action required?
options: Start and leave the file unserved for a later start
Start only after quarantining the file
open_points.default_guess: Start and leave the file unserved for a later start, matching failed spool-directory cleanup.

open_points.subject: lifetime of unreferenced value bytes
open_points.text: Rule 3 says unreferenced value bytes are reused “until the next start removes them”, while the new parenthetical says cleanup means “only trial fixtures and named values outlive a run”; K-10 also says “The only files the kernel keeps beyond a run are the file fixtures of trial cases.”
open_points.question: May unreferenced value bytes left by a failed call remain after the associated run ends until the next process start, or must they be removed when the run ends so that they do not outlive it?
options: They may remain until the next start
They must be removed when the run ends
The ‘outlive a run’ statement applies only after start-up cleanup, not continuously
open_points.default_guess: They may remain until the next start; interpret the ‘outlive a run’ statement as describing retained, reachable content after start-up cleanup.
